subject: Transportation Systems
title: Celestial Navigation
description: A quick, practical guide to Celestial Navigation.

hook.text: For centuries, sailors found their position by measuring the angle between stars and the horizon.

buildup.text: A sextant measures this angle to within a fraction of a degree. That gives you your latitude.

discovery.text: Longitude was the hard part. Until accurate clocks existed, east-west position was mostly guesswork.

twist.text: John Harrison's marine chronometer solved longitude in the 1760s. Navigation went from art to science.

climax.text: Today GPS handles everything, but naval officers still learn celestial navigation—in case screens fail.

punchline.text: Sailors navigated oceans with a mirror and the stars.

quiz.question: What instrument do sailors use to measure star angles?
